newsitem.title: USA: Ohio corn, soybean ratings improve with rains.
newsitem.headline: Ohio corn, soybean ratings improve with rains.

text.p: Corn and soybean crop ratings improved after mild temperatures and beneficial rains in the week ended Sunday, July 6, according to the weekly crop update from the Ohio Agricultural Statistics Service.

Corn was rated 66 percent good to excellent, up from 63 percent at the level last week and compared to 37 percent last year. Average development for most of the state's corn is at 7 to 8 leaves fully emerged, it said.

Soybeans were rated 60 percent good to excellent, up from 56 last week and compared to 41 at that level a year earlier. Blooming was up to 10 percent of acreage from one last week and the pace was still a week ahead of last year's crop.

Winter wheat ratings slipped to 62 percent good to excellent from 65 last week and compared to 25 percent at the same level a year earlier. Wheat was turning color on 89 percent of acres and was ripe on 4 percent, the agency said.
Wheat growth 3was 3 to 9 days behind the 5-year averages.
Oats were rated 52 percent good to excellent, versus 53 last week and 37 last year.
Pastures were rated 62 percent good to excellent, versus 64 percent last week and 51 percent last year.
Livestock were reported in mostly good to excellent condition, with some concerns about stress from the heat.
Soil moisture ratings rose with the week's rains, with topsoils rated 24 percent surplus versus 10 last week and 73 percent adequate versus 78 last week.
